name: Republic of Genoa
alt: Duchy of Genoa (1458-1461, under John of Anjou)

predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire
predecessors.text: Genoa and its Ligurian coast, the city that 'adopted a constitution' as the Compagna Communis at the end of the 11th century

successors.name: Ligurian Republic
successors.text: the Republic of Genoa's territory, proclaimed the Ligurian Republic under French oversight on 14 June 1797

ledger.x: 1099: Genoa constitutes itself as the Compagna Communis.
By 1200 the whole Ligurian coast is Genoese.
1202: Genoa holds the southern tip of Corsica.
1248: the Genoese seize Rhodes.
1248: Rhodes, 'a dependency of the Empire of Nicaea', is attacked; 'Kantakouzenos set out in late 1248 or early 1249'; the Achaean prince arrived 'in about the middle of May 1249'.
Late 1249 or early 1250: the Genoese surrender Rhodes.
Late 1249 or early 1250: the Genoese surrender.
1259: the Doria and Malaspina take over Logudoro as Genoese influence.
1266: Caffa is granted to the Genoese and becomes the capital of Gazaria.
1275: Chios (with Samos) is granted to Genoa by Byzantium.
1282: Pisa tries to take Corsica from Genoa.
1284: Genoa takes Elba after Meloria.
5 August 1284: Genoa wins the naval Battle of Meloria and Corsica passes to it.
1284: Corsica falls to Genoa.
1292: Pisa regains Elba.
8 January 1297: François Grimaldi's reign on the Rock begins (List of rulers of Monaco: reign start '8 January 1297').
10 April 1301: the Rock is back under Genoese control.
1304: Chios passes from the Republic's own hold to the Zaccaria lordship.
1305: three cells appear on the Taman side of the Kerch Strait.
1306: the Genoese and Trebizond fall out.
1308: the Golden Horde takes Caffa.
1313: Genoa regains Caffa.
1314: peace. 'Eventually the two parties made peace, confirmed in a surviving treaty from 1314 and another from 1316'; the page does not say who signed.
1316: Genoa founds La Tana at the mouth of the Don.
12 September 1331: Charles I Grimaldi 'retook the Rock from the Genoese' (List of rulers of Monaco).

12 September 1346: the Genoese Maona takes Chios and holds it as a Genoese chartered company, drawn as a vassal tint of the Republic (the maona-of-chios dossier is type colony, 12 September 1346 to April 1566).
1347: the Genoese seize Kerasus.

1349: end of the Genoese hold of Kerasus, bridged: the Empire of Trebizond page gives no end and the Alexios III page links the Genoese only to Leonkastron in 1349; the year is the empire-of-trebizond dossier's.
1349: Leonkastron is conceded to the Genoese.
1354: the Catalans occupy Alghero and the Doria lordships end.
1354: the Genoese conquer Tripoli.
1355: Tripoli is handed to the Banu Makki.
15 August 1357: 'Under Genoese control from 15 August 1357 to January 1395'; Charles I's reign ends '15 August 1357'.
19 July 1365: the Genoese of Caffa seize Soldaia.
1372: Genoa seizes Famagusta.
1372: the Kingdom of Cyprus becomes a tributary of Genoa.
1375: the Crimean coast widens to the rest of the Gothia coast (Cembalo; Soldaia has its own 1365 event).
1394: the French dominate Genoa.
January 1395: the Genoese control ends 'to January 1395' and Louis Grimaldi reigns from January 1395 (no cause given).
19 December 1395: 'Under Genoese control from 19 December 1395 to 11 May 1397'; Louis's first reign ends 19 December 1395.
11 May 1397: Louis reigns again from '11 May 1397', the Genoese control ending that day.
5 November 1402: 'Under Genoese control from 5 November 1402 to 5 June 1419'; Louis's second reign ends '5 November 1402'.
1405: Livorno is sold to the Republic of Genoa.
1409: French domination of Genoa ends.
5 June 1419: 'Sons of Rainier II, Jean, Ambroise and Antoine, bought back Monaco from Genoa' (List of rulers of Monaco).
1421: Genoa passes to Milan.
28 August 1421: Florence buys Livorno.
1422: Aragon holds Corsica.
1426: Cyprus ceases to be tributary to Genoa.
February 1433: Cembalo rises against the Genoese with Theodoro's backing.
June 1434: 'A Genoese force reconquered Cembalo in June 1434'; 'Cembalo revolted once more in 1439' (page).
27 December 1435: Genoa throws off Milan.
1450: Corsica returns to Genoa.
1458: the doge hands Genoa to the French.
1461: the Republic is restored after the French handover of 1458.
1464: Milan conquers Genoa.
1464: Famagusta leaves Genoese hands.
1475: the Ottomans take the Black Sea colonies.
1478: Genoa leaves Sforza rule.
1488: Ludovico Sforza's Milan holds Genoa again.
1499: the Sforza lose Genoa.
1499: the French occupy Genoa.
1528: Andrea Doria expels the French.
1540: Genoa takes Tabarka.
August 1553: a Franco-Ottoman force invades Corsica.
1559: France returns Corsica.
April 1566: the Ottomans take Chios and the Maona's tint ends.
1580: the Republic styles itself 'Serenìscima Repùbrica de Zêna'.
20 August 1713: the Marquisate of Finale passes to Genoa.
1729: Corsica rises against Genoa.
1742: Tabarka is lost.
September 1746: the Austrians take Genoa.
1748: the Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle lets Genoa keep its lands.
1755: the Corsican Republic is proclaimed.
1755: Genoa keeps only the coastal citadels of Corsica.
1767: 'Corsica took the island of Capraia from the Genoese' (Corsican Republic page).
15 May 1768: Genoa cedes Corsica to France.
15 May 1768: the Treaty of Versailles 'established that France would return to Genoa the possession of neighboring Capraia island'.
14 June 1797: the Republic of Genoa ends.

wars.name: Genoese venture on Crete (Pescatore and da Costa)
wars.outcome: Enrico Pescatore, 'Count of Malta', took 'large parts of Crete' from 1206; Venice's attack of 1207 failed, but it 'took them until 1212 to evict Pescatore' and 'Only on 11 May 1217 did the war with Genoa end in a treaty that left Crete securely in Venetian…

wars.name: Genoese occupation of Rhodes
wars.outcome: 'The Genoese took possession of the city and island, a dependency of the Empire of Nicaea, in a surprise attack in 1248' and surrendered 'either in late 1249 or early 1250'.

wars.name: Genoese-Pisan war over Corsica (Battle of Meloria)
wars.outcome: Genoa won the naval Battle of Meloria on 5 August 1284 (Republic page) and 'it fell to Genoa in 1284, following the battle of Meloria against Pisa'.

wars.name: Genoese-Trebizond dispute over Daphnous
wars.outcome: After Alexios II 'refused the Genoese demands for further concessions in 1306' there was fighting ('the Genoese set fire to the suburbs of Trebizond'); peace was 'confirmed in a surviving treaty from 1314 and another from 1316'.

wars.name: Siege of Caffa by Toqta
wars.outcome: The Golden Horde under Toqta conquered Caffa after a lengthy siege in 1308; the Genoese regained it by 1313.

wars.name: Genoese conquest of Chios and Phocaea (the Maona)
wars.outcome: A Genoese fleet under Simone Vignoso invaded and the castle of Chios surrendered on 12 September; the Maona, controlled by the Giustiniani, held the island.

wars.name: Siege of Caffa by Jani Beg
wars.outcome: The Golden Horde under Jani Beg 'again besieged Caffa'; the page records no change of hands and links the siege to the spread of the Black Death.

wars.name: Genoese seizure of Famagusta
wars.outcome: 'In 1372 the port was seized by Genoa'; the Kingdom of Cyprus became 'Tributary state of the Republic of Genoa (1372-1426)'.

wars.name: War of Chioggia
wars.outcome: 'The War of Chioggia ended in a Genoese defeat in 1380', which 'pushed it out of eastern Mediterranean markets'.

wars.name: Theodoro's attacks on the Genoese coast (Gothia, Cembalo)
wars.outcome: 'In 1423 prince Alexios attacked and the Genoese had to spend a large sum of money to repel him'; 'Alexios supported a Greek rebellion in Cembalo in February 1433' and 'A Genoese force reconquered Cembalo in June 1434'.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Gazaria
wars.outcome: The Ottomans 'conquered' the Genoese domains in 1474 (infobox 1471-1475); the Republic page has them 'lost to the Ottoman Empire' in 1475.

wars.name: French occupation of Genoa and Andrea Doria's revolt
wars.outcome: 'Under nearly continual French occupation' from 1499; Spanish forces 'captured the city on May 30, 1522'; in 1528 Andrea Doria allied with Charles V and ousted the French.

wars.name: Franco-Ottoman invasion of Corsica
wars.outcome: A Franco-Ottoman force took Corsica from August 1553; 'By the Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis in 1559, the French returned Corsica to Genoa.'

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Chios
wars.outcome: 'In April 1566, the island of Chios was captured by the Ottoman Empire' after surrendering to Piyale Pasha.

wars.name: French-Savoyard invasion of 1625
wars.outcome: 'In May 1625, a French-Savoian army invaded the republic' and was driven out; no territory changed hands.

wars.name: Bombardment of Genoa
wars.outcome: 'In May 1684, as a punishment for Genoese support for Spain, the city was subjected to a French naval bombardment.'

wars.name: Corsican revolt and the Corsican Republic
wars.outcome: The revolt of 1729 led to Paoli's Corsican Republic in 1755 and, in 1768, the cession of Corsica by Genoa to France ('an open treaty with Genoa ceded Corsica to France in perpetuity').

wars.name: Genoa in the War of the Austrian Succession
wars.outcome: On 26 June 1745 the Republic declared war on the Kingdom of Sardinia; it surrendered to the Austrians in September 1746, who returned and besieged the city in 1747; 'The Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle let Genoa keep its lands' (1748).

wars.name: French conquest of Liguria and the Ligurian Republic
wars.outcome: After Napoleon's army defeated Austria and Piedmont in 1796, the Genoese Jacobins overthrew the old elites in June 1797 and the Ligurian Republic was proclaimed on 14 June 1797.

certainty.note: Communal-era and later frontiers on the Ligurian Riviera are approximate in the pages read, and the overseas holdings (Caffa, Tana, Chios, Corsica's coast) are points and coasts; Corsica fell by battle (Meloria 1284), not by treaty.
Sharp only where a treaty fixes the line: Corsica returned by the Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis in 1559, Genoa's lands kept at Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748, Corsica ceded by the Treaty of Versailles in 1768.
